title: The buyer's first-touch entry is dark on any production or gated deploy — landing unserved, /api/demo fail-closed by default
expected: Journey DoD: the guided sim is 'reachable WITHOUT auth or AI keys — the buyer's reachability strength'. Helena lands on the marketing page, clicks 'Watch the live demo', and the keyless run plays.
got: The full chain exists in code (SparkLanding CTA → /api/demo → /?sim=auto → auto-start) but only on a dev/open deploy. In production the dev gate is off, '/' always mounts the dashboard, and the landing with the demo CTA is served at NO URL (/landing redirects to /). Even with the /api/demo URL in hand, a gated deploy (KP_SECRET set) refuses to mint the anonymous demo session unless KP_DEMO_ENABLED/KP_MULTI_WORKSPACE is set — the default redirects to '/' with no session and no sim. The lock itself is an honest, documented fail-safe (the anon session could read real tenant PII through ~28 still-unscoped tables), but the net effect is that the product's best pre-sales asset is invisible to the buyer it was built for. Severity derived blocker for the buyer journey, dropped one level per rubric because the darkness is deliberate and documented ('top-of-funnel is dark on purpose').

scope_note: Unlaunched-by-design and documented (docs/DESIGN.md 'Public landing' per the code comments); NOT in accepted-gaps.md, so it surfaces here as the ship-bar evidence: the buyer journey is dev-only until the landing launches and KP_DEMO_ENABLED (or full tenancy) opens the demo entry.

suggested_acceptance: Launch checklist: gate '/' on the real auth cookie (isOperator), serve the landing to signed-out prod visitors, and enable the demo entry on a deploy with no real candidate data (KP_DEMO_ENABLED=1) or completed tenancy scoping.

title: The SimBar is collapsed by default and never auto-expands — the climax CTA ends the auto-play run invisible, and an About-tab start (step mode) waits on a 'Next' the user can't see

got: SimBar's panel starts collapsed (useState(true)) and the only thing that expands it is a click on the pill. Nothing expands it when a run starts, pauses at a step gate, or finishes. Consequences: (a) Helena's auto-play entry (?sim=auto, play mode) finishes with status 'Done — candidate hired 🎉' and the 'Get started — do it with your roles' CTA rendered inside the translated-away panel — the viewer sees only the small pill; (b) Petra's About-tab / palette starts run in step mode by default (stepRef=true), so the walk immediately blocks on gate() awaiting a Next button that is hidden in the collapsed panel — a frozen-looking demo on the very first manual run. The overlays (spotlight, drawer) carry the show, but every control, the status line, the log, and the conversion CTA are behind the pill.

title: The demo's screen wave dispatches REAL rejection comms for auto-rejected pool candidates — nothing sandboxes the comms channel in sim mode
expected: Journey precondition: 'the sim uses its own seeded company template + sim store, NOT the tenant's real candidate data' — and Petra's goal is a demo that never touches candidates. A guided demo should not emit candidate-facing communications.
got: The sim sources REAL candidates from the live pool (listMatrixProfiles) into the (SIM) job, then commits a real screen wave that auto-rejects the bottom ~25% and calls dispatchRejection per rejected candidate — which routes through the live comms channel. Keyless dev = a terminal local outbox row (honest 'queued' contract), so today's containment is real but ENVIRONMENTAL: no code path disables or sandboxes comms for sim entries. On a deploy with COMMS_WEBHOOK_URL configured (real delivery is a closed gap per the comms work), a stakeholder demo would relay genuine rejection messages — plus the interview confirmation, offer, and onboarding comms for the walked candidate — to real candidates about a job titled '… (SIM)' they never applied to. The demo-workspace isolation does not catch this either: comms/pipeline tables are among the workspace-blind ~28 (workspace-lock.ts), which is exactly why the demo session is fail-closed on gated deploys.

title: STRENGTH — no silent success, no fake success: labelled halts, honest timeout notices, and an invariant-pinned demo coupling
got: Every phase logs what happened and to whom ('Live · sourced 5 candidates → Accepted', 'Screening wave · 2 auto-rejected (with rationale), 4 advanced · early-career protected', 'Offer sent · secure link generated'). Expected-transition timeouts THROW labelled messages that halt the demo legibly instead of walking on stale state (waitEntry/advanceTo failure policy, documented at the call sites); a group-eval that can't finish in 25s renders an explicit 'couldn't be generated in time' notice in the reused real modal rather than a blank comparison; a transient 500 from the pipeline fetch throws instead of being coerced into an empty board. The two silently-coupled magic numbers that could break the walk (inbound score floor vs reject ceiling) are single-sourced into SIM_SCREEN_POLICY with a fail-fast module-load assert AND a CI test.
